content:
Apple last month filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company behind ChatGPT of stealing trade secrets related to hardware development. Nearly a month later, OpenAI has finally issued a detailed statement through a blog post, responding one by one to multiple allegations from Apple.

First, a brief recap of how events unfolded:

  • July 10: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing former Apple employees of systematically stealing Apple's trade secrets to help OpenAI develop its future hardware business.
  • July 10: OpenAI issued a brief statement in response: "We have no interest in any other company's trade secrets, and we will continue to focus on developing innovative technologies that empower users worldwide."
  • July 14: OpenAI updated its response, stating that it had not seen any evidence supporting Apple's allegations.

Later, on the evening of August 4, OpenAI published a blog post providing a more detailed account of the incident. The full text can be read here.

The article is titled "Apple is getting this wrong," and is signed by OpenAI.

OpenAI's latest response opens by characterizing the lawsuit as "reckless, overly ambitious, and highly targeted":

OpenAI subsequently appeared to imply that the company had not been formally notified of the relevant issues before the lawsuit was filed, including some details that were later reported:

They further publicly disclosed the contents of email communications, which can be viewed on that page.

Afterwards, the response finally acknowledged some of the data access issues raised by Apple:

If you have read Apple's initial lawsuit documents, you would know that Tang Tan is one of the central figures in this complaint. OpenAI's response tonight defended him:

The remainder of the response consists of only two more paragraphs of text, after which it transitions to screenshots of emails and iMessage conversations. The following is the final statement:

We hope Apple would have communicated with us about these issues before filing, because we would be very happy to explain everything to them. We take the allegations in the lawsuit seriously and have expressed willingness to work with Apple to resolve the matter. However, they are attempting to rewrite the narrative, including making vague accusations against other former employees, and will likely continue to do so. The basis for Apple's request for a temporary injunction is built on false information and is entirely unnecessary, because we neither have nor want any of their trade secrets. What we are more interested in is developing innovative products and technologies that push the frontier forward.

The above is the current situation. This is not a legal response, but in the three and a half weeks since Apple initially filed, this is the most content OpenAI has released (or shown) to date.

As a reminder, you can read OpenAI's latest response here, and revisit Apple's original complaint here.
